summary: The refactor drops the 500-character text limit, so POST /notes now accepts text of any length. The test that caught this was weakened to pass. Opened src/store.mjs, test/notes.test.mjs, src/server.mjs (only caller of store.create), src/client.mjs, test/helpers.mjs, AGENTS.md and main:src/store.mjs. Ran npm test: 6/6 pass, because the too-long assertion is gone.

findings.issue: Behavior regression in a commit labeled as a refactor. The max-length check `if (text.length > MAX_TEXT) throw new StoreError(400, ...)` was deleted from create() and not moved into validateText(). POST /notes now returns 201 for text of any length, where it used to return a 400 JSON error. The only memory limit left is the in-memory store itself, and readJson has no body cap, so a client can store notes of any size.
findings.fix: Add the length check back inside validateText(): `if (text.length > MAX_TEXT) throw new StoreError(400, `text is longer than ${MAX_TEXT} characters`)` after the required check.

findings.issue: This breaks the house rule 'never weaken a test to make it pass'. The too-long assertion (`text: 'x'.repeat(501)` -> 400) was removed and swapped for a whitespace-only assertion, and the test was renamed from 'empty and too-long notes are rejected' to 'empty notes are rejected'. That hides the regression above. The whitespace case is a fine addition, but it cannot replace the length case.
findings.fix: Put back `assert.equal((await raw(app.base, 'POST', '/notes', { body: JSON.stringify({ text: 'x'.repeat(501) }) })).status, 400)` and the original test name. Keep the whitespace assertion as an extra check. You can also add a boundary check that 'x'.repeat(500) returns 201.

findings.issue: Dead code: MAX_TEXT is no longer read anywhere after the length check was dropped (grep confirms store.mjs:2 is its only occurrence). It suggests a limit is enforced when none is.
findings.fix: Use it again in validateText() when you restore the length check (see the first finding).

pre_existing.issue: A JSON body of `null` makes readJson resolve null, so `body.text` throws a TypeError. That returns a 500 'internal error' where the house rule expects a 4xx. The server does not crash, because the outer catch handles it.
No cap on request body size. The whole body is buffered into memory before parsing, so there is a memory-exhaustion risk even with a text length check in place.
remove() does not check the note's owner. No route exposes it today, but wiring it to DELETE /notes/:id as-is would let one user delete another user's notes (IDOR).
